name: Captain's Chair Straight-Leg Raise
aliases: Straight leg raise on power tower
Vertical knee/leg raise station straight leg raise
movementPattern: Hip flexion and posterior pelvic tilt - suspended forearm support
grip: Forearms supported on padded horizontal rests with hands gripping vertical stabilization handles.
description: Support bodyweight on forearms in a captain's chair tower and elevate straight legs forward and upward to horizontal or above, engaging the hip flexors and curling the pelvis into posterior tilt to recruit the rectus abdominis.
setup: Step into the captain's chair tower and mount the padded forearm rests.
Grip the upright handles firmly and allow your legs to hang freely beneath you with back flat against the backrest pad.
Depress your shoulders away from your ears to maintain active upper-body stability.
instructions: Raise both legs straight out in front of you without swinging or bending knees.
Continue lifting until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor (90 degrees at hips), curling the pelvis upward slightly at the peak.
Hold for a brief pause at peak contraction.
Lower your legs slowly under control back to the hanging vertical position before initiating the next rep.
cues: Keep legs straight and toes pointed.
Do not swing legs from the bottom.
Roll the pelvis upward at the top.
commonMistakes: Using swinging momentum to kick the legs up.
Letting shoulders shrug upward into the neck.
Arching the lumbar spine away from the backrest at the bottom.

variantNote: Straight-leg variant of the captain's chair raise. Longer lever arm significantly increases torque and abdominal recruitment compared to bent-knee variations.
